bench: BENCH-D write/commit-freshness contract (achievable core; no Kafka/Flink front)
purpose: Independent reproduction of the two owner-input-free arms (file-write Iceberg + SQL-transaction DuckLake) to move MDR-0026 file-write + SQL-transaction arms HOLD -> partial-DONE. Never-write/ISK arm remains owner-gated (Streambased access).
reproducibility_basis: Synthetic conn-like corpus, seed pinned random.seed(7); harness reports median of 3 reps per batch; two independent process runs per arm on 2026-06-28; cross-checked against the 2026-06-15 baseline (results/bench_d.json). DuckLake arm fully local; Iceberg arm in-container on ejs-bench_ejs network (Nessie REST + MinIO), internal endpoints.
verdict: Both arms reproduce the 2026-06-15 bands within run-to-run noise ~3 weeks later. Write/commit ordering stable: DuckLake (SQL-transaction) < Iceberg (file-write) at every batch; both sub-second. The divergence is read-after-write (DuckLake single-digit ms vs Iceberg ~130-344 ms), matching the original finding.
remaining_owner_gated: never-write / virtual-view arm (Streambased ISK) — requires vendor access; not runnable on-box. Per MDR-0026 owner brief, that arm not closing means the metadata_realization criterion stays HOLD-PROPOSED.
